It centralises the repetitive JSON unmarshal used by existence\n// checks across the codebase.\nfunc queryExists(sql string) (bool, error) {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(sql)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tvar rows []struct {\n\t\tOne int `json:\"1\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &rows); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\treturn len(rows) > 0, nil\n}\n\n// queryRows runs a query and unmarshals the JSON result set into dest, which\n// must be a pointer to a slice. It is\n// used by idempotent migration functions to decide whether to run ALTER TABLE.\nfunc tableHasColumn(table, column string) (bool, error) {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(fmt.Sprintf(\"PRAGMA table_info(%s);\", table))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tvar cols []struct {\n\t\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &cols); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tfor _, c := range cols {\n\t\tif c.Name == column {\n\t\t\treturn true, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false, nil\n}\n\n// dbExec runs a SQL statement through the sqlite3 CLI. The bool result indicates\n// whether a version row exists at all.\nfunc queryVersion() (int, bool, error) {\n\tvar rows []struct {\n\t\tVersion int `json:\"version\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := queryRows(`SELECT version FROM schema_version LIMIT 1;`, &rows); err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0, false, err\n\t}\n\tif len(rows) == 0 {\n\t\treturn 0, false, nil\n\t}\n\treturn rows[0].Version, true, nil\n}\n\n// writeJSON writes a JSON response with the given status code. Encoding errors\n// are logged but never returned to the client, so the response is already\n// committed by the time an error can be detected.\nfunc writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, body any) {\n\tw.Header().Set(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n\tw.WriteHeader(status)\n\tif err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(body); err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Printf(\"encode error: %v\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\n// writeError writes the standard error envelope used by every handler in this\n// service. It preserves the exact error messages required by the cumulative\n// evaluator suite, so callers should pass the same message strings that were\n// used in the original implementation.\nfunc writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, message string) {\n\twriteJSON(w, status, map[string]any{\"error\": message})\n}\n\n// healthHandler reports that the server is running. It does not exercise the\n// database, so it can be used as a liveness check.\nfunc healthHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{\"ok\": true})\n}\n\n// storageStatusHandler returns the storage driver and schema version. If the\n// schema_version table has not been initialized yet, it still reports version 1\n// but with initialized=false.\nfunc storageStatusHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n\tversion, ok, err := queryVersion()\n\tif err != nil || !ok {\n\t\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{\"driver\": \"sqlite\", \"schema_version\": 1, \"initialized\": false})\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{\"driver\": \"sqlite\", \"schema_version\": version, \"initialized\": true})\n}\n\n// storageResetHandler drops all game tables and recreates the schema from scratch.\n// The users table is preserved so that authenticated play-surface tests can\n// reuse accounts created by earlier auth tests. This is intended for test\n// isolation and deterministic replays.\nfunc storageResetHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n\tdbMu.Lock()\n\tdefer dbMu.Unlock()\n\n\tif err := dbExec(gameTablesDropSQL + schemaSQL); err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Printf(\"storage reset error: %v\", err)\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, \"reset failed\")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{\"ok\": true, \"schema_version\": 1})\n}\n\n// migrateCharacterSpellsTable creates the character_spells table if it does\n// not yet exist. must still hold dbMu for reads and writes that use this helper.\nfunc sq(s string) string {\n\treturn \"'\" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, \"'\", \"''\") + \"'\"\n}\n\n// queryExists runs a SELECT 1 style query and reports whether any row was\n// returned. It centralises the repetitive JSON unmarshal used by existence\n// checks across the codebase.\nfunc queryExists(sql string) (bool, error) {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(sql)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tvar rows []struct {\n\t\tOne int `json:\"1\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &rows); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\treturn len(rows) > 0, nil\n}\n\n// queryRows runs a query and unmarshals the JSON result set into dest, which\n// must be a pointer to a slice. An empty result is unmarshaled as an empty\n// slice, matching the contract of dbQuery.\nfunc queryRows(sql string, dest any) error {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(sql)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\treturn json.Unmarshal(out, dest)\n}\n\n// tableHasColumn reports whether a column exists in the named table. It is\n// used by idempotent migration functions to decide whether to run ALTER TABLE.\nfunc tableHasColumn(table, column string) (bool, error) {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(fmt.Sprintf(\"PRAGMA table_info(%s);\", table))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tvar cols []struct {\n\t\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &cols); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tfor _, c := range cols {\n\t\tif c.Name == column {\n\t\t\treturn true, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false, nil\n}\n\n// dbExec runs a SQL statement through the sqlite3 CLI. It is used for DDL,\n// DML, and any operation that does not need a result set.\nfunc dbExec(sql string) error {\n\tcmd := exec.Command(\"sqlite3\", dbPath, sql)\n\tvar stderr bytes.Buffer\n\tcmd.Stderr = &stderr\n\tif err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"sqlite3 exec: %v: %s\", err, stderr.String())\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// dbQuery runs a SQL query through the sqlite3 CLI and returns the JSON\n// result set. An empty result is normalized to the JSON array \"[]\" so that\n// callers always receive a consistent array representation.\nfunc dbQuery(sql string) ([]byte, error) {\n\tcmd := exec.Command(\"sqlite3\", \"-json\", dbPath, sql)\n\tvar stderr bytes.Buffer\n\tcmd.Stderr = &stderr\n\tout, err := cmd.Output()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"sqlite3 query: %v: %s\", err, stderr.String())\n\t}\n\tif len(out) == 0 {\n\t\treturn []byte(\"[]\"), nil\n\t}\n\treturn out, nil\n}\n\n// initDB creates the schema and marks the current schema version. It returns the authenticated\n// username on success. On failure it writes a 401 or 403 response and returns\n// false, so the caller should return immediately.\n//\n// A well-formed session token whose username is not present in the users table\n// is treated as a non-member and receives 403, matching the benchmark's\n// reference-server semantics.\nfunc requireDM(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (string, bool) {\n\tusername, ok := bearerUsername(r)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, \"unauthorized\")\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\n\tuser, ok, err := loadUserByUsername(username)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Printf(\"play auth query error: %v\", err)\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, \"internal error\")\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\tif !ok || user.Role != \"dm\" {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusForbidden, \"forbidden\")\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\treturn username, true\n}\n\n// requirePlayer authenticates the request using the session bearer token and\n// authorizes only users with the \"player\" role. It returns the authenticated\n// username on success. On failure it writes a 401 or 403 response and returns\n// false, so the caller should return immediately.\nfunc requirePlayer(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (string, bool) {\n\tusername, ok := bearerUsername(r)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, \"unauthorized\")\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\n\tuser, ok, err := loadUserByUsername(username)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Printf(\"play auth query error: %v\", err)\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, \"internal error\")\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\tif !ok || user.Role != \"player\" {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusForbidden, \"forbidden\")\n\t\treturn \"\", false\n\t}\n\treturn username, true\n}\n\n// requireCampaignOwnerOrMember authenticates the request using the session\n// bearer token and authorizes only the campaign owner or a campaign member.\n// It returns the authenticated username on success. State, persistence, and routing design\n\n### Persistence\n\n- All durable state lives in a single SQLite file, `game.db`, in the working\n  directory.\n- The application uses the `sqlite3` command-line tool via `os/exec`. It does\n  **not** use a Go SQLite driver or connection pool.\n- Because every query spawns a new process, all database reads and writes are\n  serialized through the `dbMu sync.Mutex` declared in `db.go`.\n- `dbExec` runs statements that return no rows (DDL, DML, DELETE).\n- `dbQuery` runs `sqlite3 -json` and returns the JSON-encoded result set; an\n  empty result is normalized to `[]`.\n- `sq` quotes string literals for SQL. Callers must acquire `dbMu` before\n  issuing queries and use `sq` for any string values.\n- `queryExists` and `queryRows` are small helpers in `db.go` that remove the\n  repetitive JSON-unmarshal boilerplate from `SELECT 1` and general queries.\n- `initDB` creates the schema from the shared `schemaSQL` constant and runs\n  migrations for older databases.\n- `POST /v1/storage/reset` drops and recreates all game tables using the same\n  `schemaSQL` script. The `users` table is intentionally preserved so that\n  authenticated tests can reuse accounts across resets.\n\n### Routing\n\n- Routes are registered with the standard library `http.ServeMux` pattern syntax\n  (e.g., `GET /health`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/{id}/advance`).\n- `r.PathValue(\"id\")` extracts path parameters.\n- The server always listens on `127.0.0.1` and uses `net.JoinHostPort` to handle\n  the `PORT` env var safely.\n\n### JSON responses\n\n- `writeJSON` sets `Content-Type: application/json` and encodes the body.\n- `writeError` is the single helper used for all error envelopes and produces\n  `{\"error\": \"...\"}`. The exact message strings are preserved from the\n  original implementation because the cumulative evaluator suite checks them.\n\n## Shared helpers and data boundaries\n\n### User identity\n\n- `bearerUsername` extracts the username from a `Bearer session-<username>`\n  header.\n- `loadUserByUsername` loads a full `User` row while the caller holds `dbMu`.\n- `requireDM` / `requirePlayer` / `requireCampaignOwner` /\n  `requireCampaignOwnerOrMember` enforce the play-surface authorization rules.\n  They return the authenticated username on success and write a 401 or 403\n  response on failure.\n\n### Play campaigns\n\n- `play.go` owns the shared request/response structs and the core play campaign\n  queries (`queryPlayCampaign`, `queryPlayCampaignMembers`, `queryPlayCampaignMember`,\n  `nextNarrationSequence`).\n- Domain-specific play files (`play_turns.go`, `play_scenes.go`, `play_locations.go`,\n  `play_encounters.go`, `play_characters.go`) import these shared types and helpers\n  and register no additional package-level state.\n- `queryPlayCampaignMembers` loads party members ordered by `join_order`.\n- `nextNarrationSequence` returns the next monotonic sequence number for a\n  campaign's narration log.\n\n### Encounter math\n\n- `computeEncounterMath` in `encounters.go` is the single source of truth for\n  encounter difficulty. Choose the file that matches the domain (or create a new file in `package main`).\n   Keep play-surface files focused: campaign creation and shared state live in\n   `play.go`, while travel, scenes, locations, encounters, and character\n   progression live in their own files.\n2. Implement the handler using `json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)` and\n   `writeJSON` / `writeError`. Reuse `writeError` with the exact error strings\n   used elsewhere if they are semantically identical.\n4. Register the route in `main.go` with the correct method and pattern.\n5.
